definitions.explanation: A shirt or garment style with the collar worn open, without a tie or buttoned-up neckline. Refers especially to the open-collar dress shirts commonly worn in summer in Japan.

examples.japanese: {開襟|かいきん}シャツを{着|き}る。
{夏場|なつば}は{開襟|かいきん}シャツで{出勤|しゅっきん}する{人|ひと}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: In summer, many people go to work in open-collar shirts.

examples.japanese: クールビズの{普及|ふきゅう}で{開襟|かいきん}スタイルが{定着|ていちゃく}した。
examples.english: The spread of Cool Biz has established the open-collar style.

notes:
Combines {開|かい} (open) + {襟|きん} (collar). Most commonly seen in the compound {開襟|かいきん}シャツ.

WATCH OUT:
Do not confuse with {解禁|かいきん} (lifting a ban), which has the same reading but different kanji and meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {開襟|かいきん}シャツ: open-collar shirt
- {開襟|かいきん}スタイル: open-collar style

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {開襟|かいきん} style became widespread in Japan after the government launched "クールビズ" (Cool Biz) in 2005, encouraging office workers to dress casually in summer to reduce air conditioning use. During the Cool Biz period (typically May–September), wearing an {開襟|かいきん}シャツ without a tie is standard in many workplaces.
